verses.en: The Lord’s message came to me:
verses.commentary:
25:1 "And the word of the Lord came to me saying. . ." This is the characteristic literary marker that a new
oracle is beginning. It is surprising that a date does not appear here, as it does in Ezek. 26:1 and 24:1. This causes the interpreter to ask if chapters 24-25
form a literary unit. From content it seems that these chapters form a unit of pronouncements regarding YHWH's coming judgment on the surrounding nations.

verses.zh: 「人子啊，你要面向亚扪人说预言，攻击他们，
verses.en: “Son of man, turn toward[NOTE:1] the Ammonites[NOTE:2] and prophesy against them.
notes: Heb “set your face toward.”
Heb “the sons of Ammon.” Ammon was located to the east of Israel.
verses.commentary:
25:2 "set your face toward" This IMPERATIVE (BDB 967, KB 1321, Qal IMPERTAIVE) is a
standard idiom of judgment (cf. Ezek. 15:7; Lev. 20:5; 26:17; Jer. 21:10; 44:11; Amos 9:4). See note at Ezek. 6:2; also note Ezek. 13:17; 20:46; 21:2;
25:2; 28:21; 29:2; 35:2; 38:2.

▣ "Ammon" All three trans-Jordan nations were relatives of Israel, Edom through Esau (cf. Gen. 36:1)
and Ammon and Moab through Lot (cf. Gen. 19:37-38).

Ammon was located south of the Jabbok River and another boundary somewhere north of the Arnon River.

Special Topic: Ammon

▣ "prophesy" This is a second IMPERATIVE (BDB 612, KB 659, Niphal IMPERATIVE,
cf. Ezek. 4:7; 6:2; 11:4; 13:2,17; 21:2,7; 25:2; 28:21; 29:2; 34:2; 35:2; 36:6; 38:2; 39:1). After the fall of Jerusalem, Ezekiel now proclaims YHWH's
judgment on the surrounding nations who supported or maybe were directly involved in Jerusalem's demise (cf. Jer. 49:1-6; Amos 1:13-15; Zeph. 2:8-9).

- Herodutus specifically mentions Nebuchadnezzar's devastation of the trans-jordan area in 582 B.C.

- Josephus mentions that it occurred five years after the fall of Jerusalem in 586 B.C.

verses.zh: 说：你们当听主耶和华的话。主耶和华如此说：我的圣所被亵渎，以色列地变荒凉，犹大家被掳掠；那时，你便因这些事说：『阿哈！』
verses.en: Say to the Ammonites, ‘Hear the word of the Sovereign Lord. This is what the Sovereign Lord says: You said “Aha!” about my sanctuary when it was desecrated, about the land of Israel when it was made desolate, and about the house of Judah when they went into exile.
verses.commentary:
25:3 "Hear" This is the third opening IMPERATIVE (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE)
in this section. One wonders if any of these nations ever heard these prophecies. They were addressed to them, but obviously they were directed
toward the exiles. They demonstrate that

- YHWH is a universal God

- YHWH is no respecter of persons

- YHWH will punish sin

- YHWH's word does come to pass

- YHWH's ultimate will will be accomplished

Special Topic: Listen/Hear (Shema)

▣ "Aha" This INTERJECTION expresses the joy of the Ammonites (cf.
Ps. 35:21,25; 40:15-16; Isa. 44:16; Ezek. 25:3; 26:2; 36:2), which is defined in Ezek. 25:6. They rejoiced over

- the sanctuary being profaned

- the land of Israel made desolate

- the house of Judah sent into exile

They may have participated in this exile (cf. 2 Kgs. 24:1-2).

verses.zh: 所以我必将你的地交给东方人为业；他们必在你的地上安营居住，吃你的果子，喝你的奶。
verses.en: So take note,[NOTE:1] I am about to make you slaves of[NOTE:2] the tribes[NOTE:3] of the east. They will make camps among you and pitch their tents among you. They will eat your fruit and drink your milk.
notes: The word הִנֵּה (hinneh, traditionally “behold”) indicates being aware of or taking notice of something and has been translated here with a verb (so also throughout the chapter).
Heb “Look, I am about to give you for a possession to.”
Heb “sons.”
verses.commentary:
25:4 "I am going to give you" The VERB (BDB 678, KB 733, Qal PARTICIPLE,
in Ezek. 25:10 Qal PERFECT with waw) is used in Ezek. 11:15 (Niphal PERFECT)
of Canaan being given to YHWH's covenant people, but because of their sin, the land will now be given to "the sons of the east."
This is similar to Canaan originally being taken away from the ten nations and given to Israel (cf. Gen. 15:12-21).

▣ "the sons of the east" This phrase occurs several times with several possible meanings.

- warriors, Ezek. 25:10; Jdg. 6:3,33

- wisemen, 1 Kgs. 4:30

- future relatives (i.e. Syria), Gen. 29:1

- nomadic Arabs from northern Arabia (Jer. 49:28)

Here it refers to Neo-Babylon, which is beyond Syria. Ezekiel has predicted that YHWH will judge His people
with an "east wind" (cf. Ezek. 17:10; 19:12; note Isa. 27:8).

Special Topic: East Wind

▣ "they will eat your fruit and drink your milk" This phrase is similar to Deut. 28:33, which describes
Israel's fate if she does not keep YHWH's covenant (cf. Isa. 1:7).

These terms are normally a prayer of thanksgiving (i.e. Ps. 128:2; Isa. 3:10), but here it is a curse.

Special Topic: Keep

Special Topic: Covenant

verses.zh: 我必使拉巴为骆驼场，使亚扪人的地为羊群躺卧之处，你们就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: I will make Rabbah a pasture for camels and Ammon[NOTE:1] a resting place for sheep. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
notes: Heb “the sons of Ammon.”
verses.commentary:
25:5 "Rabbah" This is the capital of Ammon located on the Wadi Amman, which becomes the Jabbok River.
This water source was the key to the city's continuity. It is the capital of the nation of Jordan today, Amman.

▣ "a pasture for camel. . .a resting place for flocks" This is a way of predicting the nation's depopulation, only nomadic
herdsmen will be there for short periods (cf. Isa. 27:10).

The term "resting place" (BDB 918) is found only here and in Zeph. 2:5 where it is used of wild beasts. This judged place
was so dry that it could only be used for grazing at certain brief times of the year.

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「因你拍手顿足，以满心的恨恶向以色列地欢喜，
verses.en: For this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Because you clapped your hands, stamped your feet, and rejoiced with intense scorn[NOTE:1] over the land of Israel,
notes: Heb “with all your scorn in (the) soul.”
verses.commentary:
25:6 The physical gestures of "clapping hands" and "stomping feet" can be understood as a way of expressing
joy or approval (cf. Ezek. 6:11; Nahum 3:19). In this context Ammon rejoiced at Judah's demise (and may have
participated in it, cf. 2 Kgs. 24:1-2).

Special Topic: Clap Your Hands

verses.zh: 所以我伸手攻击你，将你交给列国作为掳物。我必从万民中剪除你，使你从万国中败亡。我必除灭你，你就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: take note—I have stretched out my hand against you, and I will hand you over as plunder[NOTE:1] to the nations. I will cut you off from the peoples and make you perish from the lands. I will destroy you; then you will know that I am the Lord.’”
notes: The translation here follows the Qere reading: בַּז (baz, “spoil, plunder”). The Kethib reading of the consonantal text, בַּג (bag), is not a word.
verses.commentary:
25:7 "I have stretched out My hand against you" This is another idiom of judgment (cf. Exod. 7:5;
15:6,12; Isa. 5:25; 9:12,17,21; 10:4; 14:27; 23:11; Jer. 6:12; 15:6; 51:25; Ezek. 6:14; 14:13; 20:33,34;
25:7,13; 35:3; Zeph. 1:4; 2:13).

Special Topic: Hand

Special Topic: Anthropomorphic Language to Describe Deity

▣ "I shall give you for spoil to the nations" Spoil (BDB 103) refers to the property of conquered nations, including even their
own people (i.e. Num. 31:32-40). This term is found several times in Ezekiel (cf. Ezek. 25:7; 26:5; 29:19; 36:4; 38:12,13).

The MT has a word that is unknown. This has been emended by changing one consonant.

- "spoil" ‒ בז (BDB 103; Qere)

- from ‒ בג (BDB 93)

Notice the things YHWH says He will do to Ammon.

- stretched out His hand against them

- gave them for spoil to the nations

- cut them off from the peoples

- made them perish from the lands

- destroyed them (cf. Ezek. 25:10)

Ammon will be no more! This is surprising in light of Jer. 49:6 (and Moab's restoration in
Jer. 48:47). This may have an eschatological orientation or simply a poetic hyperbole.

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「因摩押和西珥人说：『看哪，犹大家与列国无异』，
verses.en: “This is what the Sovereign Lord says: ‘Moab[NOTE:1] and Seir say, “Look, the house of Judah is like all the other nations.”
notes: Moab was located immediately south of Ammon.
verses.commentary:
25:8-11 This chapter addresses

- Ammon, Ezek. 25:1-7

- Moab, Ezek. 25:8-11

- Edom, Ezek. 25:12-14

- Philistia, Ezek. 25:15-17

▣ "Moab" This is another trans-Jordan country from Lot's incestuous children by his own daughters
(cf. Genesis 19). There are several prophecies against Moab (cf. Num. 21:27-30; Isaiah 15-16; Jeremiah 48;
Amos 2:1-3; Zeph. 2:8-11). Moab's boundaries are from the Arnon River to the Brook Zered.

Special Topic: Moab

▣ "Seir" This (BDB 973) refers to a mountain range running parallel to the Arabah (see
The Zondervan Pictorial Encyclopedia of the Bible, vol. 5, pp. 329-330). It was originally the
homeland of Horite settlers (cf. Gen. 36:20-30), but they were defeated by Esau (cf. Deut. 2:12,22). Therefore,
"Seir," "Mount Seir," became ways of referring to Edomites (cf. 2 Chr. 20:10; 25:11). Edom is located south
of the Brook Zered and extends down the eastern side of the Arabah.

Special Topic: Edom and Israel

25:8 "the house of Judah is like all the nations" This statement, in one sense, was surely true. Judah
had taken up the Canaanite religion. In another sense the phrase depreciates Judah's unique relationship with
YHWH (i.e. Gen. 12:1-3; Exod. 19:4-5). These trans-jordan relative nations saw nothing different, unique,
or respectable in Judah or her God.

It is also possible that Marduk (i.e. chief god of Babylon) was seen as being stronger than the
gods of the nations which were conquered. It was Judah's military defeat that precipitated the accusations
and slurs.

Special Topic: Marduk

verses.zh: 所以我要破开摩押边界上的城邑，就是摩押人看为本国之荣耀的伯・耶西末、巴力・免、基列亭，
verses.en: So look, I am about to open up Moab’s flank,[NOTE:1] eliminating the cities,[NOTE:2] including its frontier cities,[NOTE:3] the beauty of the land—Beth Jeshimoth, Baal Meon, and Kiriathaim.
notes: Heb “shoulder.”
Heb “from the cities.” The verb “eliminating” has been added in the translation to reflect the privative use of the preposition (see BDB 583 s.v. מִן 7.b).
Heb “from its cities, from its end.”
verses.commentary:
25:9 "Beth-jeshimoth" This Moabite city was located on the eastern side of the Jordan in the ancient tribal
allocation of Reuben (cf. Josh. 12:3; 13:20). The name means "place of the desert" (BDB 111).

▣ "Baal-meon" This Moabite city was also located in the ancient tribal allocation of Reuben
(cf. Num. 32:28; Josh. 13:17; also note Jer. 48:23). Note it carries the name of the Canaanite male
fertility deity.

▣ "Kiriathaim" This is also a Moabite town in the tribal allocation of Reuben (cf. Num. 32:37;
Josh. 13:19), located on the tableland. It is also mentioned in YHWH's judgment on Moab in Jer. 48:1.

verses.zh: 好使东方人来攻击亚扪人。我必将亚扪人之地交给他们为业，使亚扪人在列国中不再被记念。
verses.en: I will hand it over,[NOTE:1] along with the Ammonites,[NOTE:2] to the tribes[NOTE:3] of the east, so that the Ammonites will no longer be remembered among the nations.
notes: Heb “I will give it for a possession.”
Heb “the sons of Ammon” (twice in this verse).
Heb “the sons.”
verses.commentary:
25:10 "Ammon may not be remembered among the nations" The VERB (BDB 269,
KB 269, Niphal IMPERFECT) is also used of Ammon in Ezek. 21:32. Ammon
will exist no more as a nation. Israel will return to its land, but Ammon will not (the same is true of Edom).

verses.zh: 我必向摩押施行审判，他们就知道我是耶和华。」
verses.en: I will execute judgments against Moab. Then they will know that I am the Lord.’”

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「因为以东报仇雪恨，攻击犹大家，向他们报仇，大大有罪，
verses.en: “This is what the Sovereign Lord says: ‘Edom[NOTE:1] has taken vengeance against the house of Judah; they have made themselves fully culpable[NOTE:2] by taking vengeance[NOTE:3] on them.[NOTE:4]
notes: Edom was located south of Moab.

Heb “and they have become guilty, becoming guilty.” The infinitive absolute following the finite verb makes the statement emphatic and draws attention to the degree of guilt incurred by Edom due to its actions.
Heb “and they have taken vengeance.”
Edom apparently in some way assisted in the destruction of Jerusalem in 587/6 b.c. (Ps 137:7; Lam 4:21, 22; Joel 3:19; Obadiah).
verses.commentary:
25:12 Edom acted against the house of Judah (cf. Ps. 137:7; Lam. 4:21-22; Obad. 1:10-14) by

- taking vengeance (BDB 667, KB 721, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT)
plus the related NOUN, BDB 668). This action caused great
guilt (Qal IMPERFECT VERB plus INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE of the
same root, BDB 79, KB 95, which is a grammatical way to show intensity).

- avenging themselves (BDB 667, KB 721, Niphal PERFECT)

Also they apparently took the opportunity of the collapse of the Judean state to annex part of her
land (cf. R. K. Harrison, Introduction to the Old Testament, p. 844).

Special Topic: Edom and Israel

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：我必伸手攻击以东，剪除人与牲畜，使以东从提幔起，人必倒在刀下，地要变为荒凉，直到底但。
verses.en: So this is what the Sovereign Lord says: I will stretch out my hand against Edom, and I will kill the people and animals within her,[NOTE:1] and I will make her desolate; from Teman to Dedan they will die[NOTE:2] by the sword.
notes: Heb “and I will cut off from her man and beast.”
Heb “fall.”
verses.commentary:
25:13-14 YHWH will respond in vengeance (BDB 668).

- stretch out His hand against them

- cut off man and beast

- lay it waste

- fall by the sword

This violation of Edom against Judah and her God (cf. Ezek. 25:8) was taken very personally by YHWH.

- My vengeance, twice (BDB 668)

- My people

- My anger

- My wrath

Note how many prophecies are against Edom (cf. Isa. 34:5-17; 63:1-6; Jer. 49:7-22; Ezek. 25:12-14;
35:1-15; Lam. 4:21-22; Amos 1:11-12; Mal. 1:2-4).

Special Topic: Edom and Israel

25:13 "Teman" This is the Hebrew word for "south," "south wind" (BDB 412). It originally designated a
grandson of Esau (cf. Gen. 36:11). It came to refer to

- the northern part of the nation of Edom (cf. Obad. 1:9; Hab. 3:3)

- a city (cf. Jer. 49:7,20; Amos 1:12)

- In this context it represents a region because it is contrasted with Dedam to designate the whole nation (similar to
the phrase "from Dan to Beersheba").

▣ "Dedan" This refers to a southern region in northwestern Arabia (cf. Gen. 10:7; 25:3). The Arab
inhabitants became identified with Edom (cf. Jer. 49:8). As an area it extended down the eastern side of the
Gulf of Aqaba.

The exact locations of Teman and Dedan are uncertain and whether they refer to a city or a
region in this context is uncertain.

verses.zh: 我必藉我民以色列的手报复以东；以色列民必照我的怒气，按我的忿怒在以东施报，以东人就知道是我施报。这是主耶和华说的。」
verses.en: I will exact my vengeance upon Edom by the hand of my people Israel. They will carry out in Edom my anger and rage; they will experience[NOTE:1] my vengeance, declares the Sovereign Lord.’”
notes: Heb “know.”
verses.commentary: 25:14 "by the hand" See Special Topic: Hand

verses.zh: 主耶和华如此说：「因非利士人向犹大人报仇，就是以恨恶的心报仇雪恨，永怀仇恨，要毁灭他们，
verses.en: “This is what the Sovereign Lord says: ‘The Philistines[NOTE:1] have exacted merciless revenge,[NOTE:2] showing intense scorn[NOTE:3] in their effort to destroy Judah[NOTE:4] with unrelenting hostility.[NOTE:5]
notes: The Philistines inhabited the coastal plain by the Mediterranean Sea, west of Judah.
Heb “have acted with vengeance and taken vengeance with vengeance.” The repetition emphasizes the degree of vengeance which they exhibited, presumably toward Judah.
Heb “with scorn in (the) soul.”
The object is not specified in the Hebrew text, but has been clarified as “Judah” in the translation.
Heb “to destroy (with) perpetual hostility.” Joel 3:4-8 also speaks of the Philistines taking advantage of the fall of Judah.
verses.commentary:
25:15 "Philistines" The Philistines were apparently Greeks from the Aegean Islands. They were the only group of people in this part of the
world who were uncircumcised. They were apparently a mercenary force who tried to attack Egypt in the twelfth century B.C. but were
defeated. They then settled on the southern coast of Palestine. They had five major city-states which are delineated in Jos.13:3: Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon,
Gath, and Ekron. They were a major military problem throughout the period of the judges and even throughout the reign of Saul and David. The name "Palestine"
comes from the word "Philistine."

Special Topic: Philistines

▣ "have acted" This verse describes Philistia's actions against YHWH's people (cf. Joel 3:4-8).

- acted in revenge

- took vengeance

- displayed scorn of soul

- destroyed with everlasting enmity (cf. Ezek. 35:5)

Wow! What strong language!

verses.zh: 所以主耶和华如此说：我必伸手攻击非利士人，剪除基利提人，灭绝沿海剩下的居民。
verses.en: So this is what the Sovereign Lord says: Take note, I am about to stretch out my hand against the Philistines. I will kill[NOTE:1] the Kerethites[NOTE:2] and destroy those who remain on the seacoast.
notes: In Hebrew the verb “and I will cut off” sounds like its object, “the Kerethites,” and draws attention to the statement.
This is a name for the Philistines, many of whom migrated to Palestine from Crete.
verses.commentary:
25:16 "Cherethites" This name is of uncertain origin (BDB 504). Two principles of hermeneutics can help here.

- In context they are parallel to Philistines. They could be a synonymous name or a specific group who were assimilated. The
Philistines were possibly Aegean people (sea peoples). The Cherethites were possibly from Crete (because of)

- Amos 9:7

- the similarity of the root consonants

- the LXX translation)

- Parallel passages link them to the Philistines (i.e. Pelethites, cf. 2 Sam. 8:18; 15:18; 20:7,23;
1 Kgs. 1:38,44; 1 Chr. 18:17; Zeph. 2:5).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible.
Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- What is the theological significance of the literary unit of Ezekiel 25-32?

- Why does Ezekiel mention the small surrounding nations first?

- Who are the Cherethites of Ezek. 25:16?

- What is the significance of the phrase "they will know that I am the Lord,"
Ezek. 25:17?

This is a study guide commentary which means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must
walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare your subject divisions with the four modern translations above. Paragraphing
is not inspired, but it is the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every paragraph has one and only one subject.

- First paragraph

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS TO CHAPTERS 25-32

- There is a subject unity (judgment on these nations) to these chapters, but not a genre uniformity. Also note the different dates.

- 9th year, 10 month, 10th day, Ezek. 24:1 (may cover chapter 25)

- 11th year, 1st month , 1st day , Ezek. 26:1

- 10th year, 10th month, 12th day, Ezek. 29:1

- 27th year, 1st month, 1st day, Ezek. 29:17

- 11th year, 1st month, 7th day, Ezek. 30:20

- 11thth year, 3rd month, 1st day, Ezek. 31:1

- 12th year, 12th month, 1st day, Ezek. 32:1

- 12th year, 12th month, 15th day, Ezek. 32:17

This clearly demonstrates that the literary unit (Ezek. 25-32) was an edited collection. By whom and when is uncertain.

- The oracles against the nations (see D.) are characteristic of Hebrew Prophetic Literature.

- Isaiah 13-21, 23, 24

- Jeremiah 46-51

- Ezekiel 25-32, 35, 38-39

- Amos 1-2

- Joel 3:1-16

- Zephaniah 2:1-3:5

- Nations to Be Judged by YHWH

- The nations listed in chapter 25 tried to get Judah to rebel against Neo-Babylon (cf. Jeremiah 27), but in the end, they benefitted,
even participated in, Judah's fall (cf. 2 Kgs. 24:1-2).

- Theological Issues

- The judgment oracles on surrounding nations and world powers of the Ancient Near East (ANE) accentuate the power, glory, and
uniqueness of Israel's God (i.e. monotheism; see Special Topic: Monotheism).

- They show that YHWH has a larger purpose for a repentant Judah. Ezekiel's prophesies of a restored, glorified temple was a way of
asserting a future hope and purpose for Israel (i.e. the Messiah). The first temple became corrupt (cf. Ezek. 8-10) and YHWH left, but
a future temple is promised (Ezek. 40-48).

- The messages of doom on the pagan nations were Ezekiel's first message of hope for God's exiled people after the exiles heard of
Jerusalem's demise (cf. Ezek. 24:25-27).

- The book of Jonah is also a condemnation of a foreign oppressor nation (i.e. Assyria). Yet, it functioned theologically as YHWH's willingness
to accept the repentance of the pagan nations (i.e. Isa. 19:23,24-25). The reality of Gen. 12:3 is being fulfilled!

Special Topic: YHWH's Eternal Redemptive Plan

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: EZEKIEL 25:1-7

1And the word of the Lord came to me saying, 2"Son
